questions.question: What does the Heine-Cantor Theorem state for a continuous function $f\colon [a,b]\to\mathbb{R}$?
questions.explanation: The Heine-Cantor Theorem states that if $f\colon[a,b]\to\mathbb{R}$ is continuous, then $f$ is uniformly continuous on $[a,b]$. Continuity on a closed bounded interval implies uniform continuity.
questions.source_support: The theorem states that a continuous function on $[a,b]$ is uniformly continuous on $[a,b]$.

option_explanations: $f$ need not be constant; e.g., $f(x)=x$ on $[0,1]$ is continuous (hence uniformly continuous) but not constant.
$f$ is continuous (hence uniformly continuous) at the endpoints too; the endpoints do not break continuity.
A continuous function on $[a,b]$ is bounded (extreme value theorem), not unbounded.
